nasa-tm-19700001369-comparison-of-tensil:
Alfred J. Nachtigall of Lewis Research Center compared two stainless steels in liquid helium in this October 1969 report. The alloys were 304L and 310S stainless steel. Both unnotched and notched specimens were tested, including welded notched pieces, with loading along and across the sheet rolling direction.

Yield strength for 310S ran nearly twice that of 304L. Ultimate tensile strength for 310S was about eighty percent of 304L in the unnotched condition. In notched tests, 310S strengths were significantly higher than 304L, welded or not. Limited tests at a still lower temperature showed no significant change. Cryogenic tanks and lines need exactly such low-temperature data.
